requirement: Write a wc-style Typer command counting newlines and words in files or stdin, continuing past unreadable files while reporting them on stderr and exiting non-zero.
skeleton: A Typer app with a wc command taking optional paths and a lines-only flag, reading stdin for none or -, catching OSError per file, printing per-input and total rows, and exiting 1 on failure.
caption: A wc clone built with Typer that counts newlines and words across several inputs and reports partial failure like the Unix tool. wc takes optional PATHS and a --lines/-l flag; with no paths, or for a path of -, it reads typer.get_text_stream of stdin, otherwise it reads the file as UTF-8. An OSError prints wc, the path and the strerror to stderr, marks the run failed and continues with the remaining inputs. Each input prints its newline count, word count unless --lines, and name separated by tabs, counting newline characters rather than lines. More than one input adds a total row. After the loop a failed run raises typer.Exit with code 1. The fixture asserts, with CliRunner, that one file has no total, that a file without a trailing newline counts one newline, the total row for two files, that stdin is read without paths and for -, and that a missing file goes to stderr, exits 1, and the other file is still counted.

plan.intent: Summarize text inputs from a shell pipeline
constraints: No paths or a dash reads standard input
Unreadable files are reported on stderr and the remaining inputs are still counted
Newline characters are counted, matching Unix wc
A total row appears only for more than one input
Any failure raises typer.Exit with code 1 after all inputs are processed

rationale.teaches: Handle per-item errors without aborting a batch, keep diagnostics on stderr, read stdin through typer.get_text_stream, and signal partial failure with typer.Exit.
rationale.why: Stopping at the first bad file hides results for the rest, errors on stdout corrupt piped output, and exiting 0 after a failure lets scripts continue with incomplete data.

ops.docstring: A Typer wc clone reading files or stdin and reporting partial failure.

candidates.why_wrong: A missing input is reported but the command still exits with code 0.
The first unreadable file aborts the run so later files are never counted.
Error messages are printed to stdout and mixed into the counts.
A single explicit file still prints a redundant total row.
A final line without a newline is counted, disagreeing with Unix wc.
